Rows are written as "field (country)". Where a profile gives one priority list for all levels, the same list is entered under each level that country offers; Fiji gives separate undergraduate and postgraduate lists and PNG gives per-level rules. Sub-fields named inside a priority area are entered as their own rows and also inside the area row.

No row lists the CRICOS register: no profile reproduces it. Vietnam, Cambodia and Mongolia profiles recommend that applicants use the CRICOS register to pick a course; the policy handbook text on CRICOS was not read in this pass.

The priority lists are the ones the governments review each year; several profiles say the examples are not limited to the fields shown (Fiji postgraduate "including but not limited to", Vietnam "examples ... not limited", Niue, Tuvalu and Tonga "including but not limited to"). Vietnam adds that studies in other fields except Business Administration are considered on merit.

Tonga priority fields (profile does not state degree levels, so not entered as rows): Governance and Economics (governance, national security, economics, public policy, public financial management, media and communications, procurement and contract management, law and accounting); Health (all clinical qualifications, community and public health, allied health particularly mental health, physiotherapy, speech therapy, occupational therapy, exercise physiology, nutrition and dietetics); Infrastructure (engineering, surveying, construction management, aviation policy and management); Sciences (energy, veterinary sciences, statistics, information technology and cyber security); Environment and natural resource management (agriculture, fisheries, water management, climate change, disaster preparedness and resilience); Education (teaching qualifications, policy and management); Community Development and Inclusion (community and social development, gender equality studies, disability inclusion).
